correctness.rationale: The ces_2^(2) norm linearly transforms to M(s,t)^2=s²+t²+(2/sqrt5)|st|. Smooth Birkhoff tangents w_z reduce the optimization to one scalar z and crossing t=1/(z+1/sqrt5), with unconstrained same-chamber extrema bounded below the candidate and post-crossing ratios decreasing; nonsmooth coordinate-axis tangent cones give at most sqrt3. The crossing profile has derivative vanishing at the unique positive root of the displayed sextic by positive-side squared equation and Descartes plus endpoint signs: z≈0.3501660338698, μ≈1.8305373425659. Independent numerical 2-variable maximization corroborated value but not continuum proof. Scope only real two-dimensional Cesaro exponent two.

originality.rationale: The same finite Cesaro norm is studied in Maligranda–Petrot–Suantai, but Section 4 computes the James constant, not the Birkhoff–James rectangular constant. Baronti–Casini–Papini's primary full rectangular text treats general results and other examples; Paul–Ghosh–Sain's polygonal reduction does not compute this smooth-nonsmooth Cesaro sphere. del Río–Benítez's authorized 1977 pages1–3 concern the two-dimensional Hilbert endpoint μ=sqrt2, not the specific Cesaro sextic. No indexed stronger exact Cesaro rectangular calculation was found; residual bibliographic access gaps remain.
